metadata.name: Baz Needs Catalogue — Bank of Ireland Personal Banking
metadata.scope: BOI personal banking in the Republic of Ireland. Business, corporate, private banking and wealth management are excluded except where a personal journey overlaps.
metadata.purpose: Turn conversational context into evidence-backed need candidates, then clarify, surface, defer or suppress BOI options.
metadata.source_policy: Live product facts, eligibility, rates, offers and scheme availability must come from controlled BOI data; never from model memory.

explicit.description: Customer directly states the need or product intent.

strong_inferred.description: Circumstances strongly suggest the need; normally clarify before surfacing.

soft_inferred.description: Supporting context only; insufficient on its own.

operating_model.principle: Evidence can suggest a need; the customer decides whether to pursue a product.

when: persistent inability to meet normal living costs
arrears or repeated missed payments disclosed
global_suppressions.reason: Do not answer structural financial difficulty with opportunistic credit.
New commitments may affect mortgage assessment.

when: money required within roughly five years
customer requires capital certainty or near-term access
global_suppressions.reason: Short-term saving and investment risk solve different problems.

when: customer discloses diagnosis/illness/treatment without asking about protection
global_suppressions.reason: Health disclosure is not a sales trigger.

when: customer explicitly declines a surfaced product
global_suppressions.action: Do not resurface unless circumstances materially change or customer asks.

when: customer asks for comparative claims about another bank
global_suppressions.action: Explain BOI options only; do not provide competitor recommendation.
global_suppressions.reason: Keep Baz within approved BOI domain.

products.name: Instant Access Demand Account / Money Pot

needs.name: Everyday banking

signals.text: I need somewhere for my salary

clarifying_questions: Is this mainly for salary, bills and everyday spending?
Are you already living in Ireland, or moving here soon?
needs.approved_framing: A current account can give you a home for salary, bills, card spending and everyday payments.

needs.name: Shared household finances

signals.text: we want an account for bills

clarifying_questions: Do you want to combine everything, or just have somewhere for shared bills and spending?
needs.approved_framing: You can keep your individual accounts and add a joint account for shared household money.

needs.name: Moving to Ireland
clarifying_questions: When are you moving?
Do you already have an Irish payment account?
needs.approved_framing: BOI has a current-account journey for people moving to Ireland; we can check what you can set up before you arrive.

needs.name: Child money skills

signals.text: first debit card for my child

clarifying_questions: How old are they?
How much control would you like to keep over spending?
needs.approved_framing: A child account can help them learn to spend and save while you keep appropriate oversight.

needs.name: Teen banking
clarifying_questions: How old are they?
Are they in second-level education?
needs.approved_framing: BOI has an account designed for second-level students.

needs.name: Third-level student banking
clarifying_questions: Are you in full-time third-level education?
Are you undergraduate or postgraduate?
needs.approved_framing: We can look at day-to-day student banking first, then any borrowing or credit needs separately.

needs.name: Graduate banking
clarifying_questions: When did you graduate?
Are you already employed or do you have an offer?
needs.approved_framing: BOI has banking and borrowing options specifically for recent graduates.

needs.name: Retirement everyday banking

signals.text: my pension is replacing my salary

clarifying_questions: Are you looking mainly for everyday banking, or do you also want to review retirement income?
needs.approved_framing: We can separate everyday banking from the bigger retirement-planning conversation.

needs.name: Basic payment account

signals.text: I just need a basic account
I don't have any payment account in Ireland

clarifying_questions: Do you currently hold another payment account in the Republic of Ireland?
needs.approved_framing: BOI has a basic payment account for eligible customers who need core everyday banking.
suppressions: Do not position as merely a cheaper current account; eligibility matters.

needs.name: Emergency / rainy-day cash
clarifying_questions: Would you need to get at this money immediately?
How much would you like to keep accessible?
needs.approved_framing: You can separate emergency cash from everyday spending while keeping it available on demand.

needs.name: Build a regular saving habit

signals.text: want to become a better saver

clarifying_questions: What are you saving for?
When do you expect to need the money?
needs.approved_framing: A regular-savings account can automate the habit; the right one depends on your goal and access needs.

needs.name: Save for a defined goal
clarifying_questions: How much do you want to build up?
When will you need it?
Do you need instant access?
needs.approved_framing: We can put the goal on a regular saving path and keep it separate from day-to-day money.

needs.name: Save a first-home deposit

signals.text: first home in a few years

clarifying_questions: Are you both first-time buyers?
Roughly when would you like to buy?
needs.approved_framing: You can build the deposit first and, when you're ready, carry the context into the mortgage journey.

needs.name: Lump sum with limited access

signals.text: I can give notice before taking it out
I won't need all of this immediately

clarifying_questions: How quickly might you need access?
Is the amount at least €5,000?
needs.approved_framing: If you can give notice before withdrawing, a notice account may suit the access pattern better than instant-access cash.

needs.name: Lump sum not needed for a fixed period

signals.text: I won't need the money for 6 to 18 months

clarifying_questions: Are you comfortable locking the money away for a fixed period?
What is the earliest date you may need it?
needs.approved_framing: If you do not need near-term access, a fixed-term deposit can give the money a defined home for that period.
suppressions: Do not surface if the customer indicates likely short-notice access needs.

needs.name: Save for a child
clarifying_questions: How old is the child?
Is this for the next few years or a longer-term goal like college?
needs.approved_framing: The key question is time horizon: shorter-term child savings and long-term investing solve different problems.
suppressions: Do not move directly into investments without horizon, affordability and risk discussion.

needs.name: Hold foreign currency
clarifying_questions: Which currency?
Do you need to hold it, or simply transfer it?
needs.approved_framing: We should first distinguish between holding foreign currency and simply sending or receiving it.

needs.name: Occasional short-term cashflow gap
clarifying_questions: Is this a one-off shortfall or something that happens regularly?
needs.approved_framing: An overdraft can provide short-term flexibility on a current account.
suppressions: Suppress borrowing cross-sell if the customer describes persistent inability to meet normal living costs.
Do not use overdraft as a solution to structural financial difficulty.

needs.name: One-off personal borrowing
clarifying_questions: How much do you need?
What is it for?
Over what period would you prefer to repay it?
needs.approved_framing: A personal loan gives you a fixed lump sum and a defined repayment term.
suppressions: If a mortgage application is active, assess whether new borrowing should be deferred before surfacing.

needs.name: Finance a car
clarifying_questions: How much are you looking to borrow?
Is the car electric, plug-in hybrid or conventional?
needs.approved_framing: BOI has car borrowing options; vehicle type may affect which route is relevant.

needs.name: Fund home improvements
clarifying_questions: Roughly how much will the work cost?
Are any of the works improving energy efficiency?
needs.approved_framing: There are unsecured and mortgage-backed routes; the size and nature of the work determine what is worth exploring.

needs.name: Improve home energy efficiency
clarifying_questions: What work are you planning?
Do you have a quote?
Is an SEAI-supported upgrade involved?
needs.approved_framing: Energy-efficiency works may qualify for dedicated borrowing routes; home cover may also need reviewing after major upgrades.
notes: Validate live availability of scheme-backed products before presentation.

needs.name: Additional borrowing on an existing BOI loan

signals.text: I already have a BOI loan and need more

clarifying_questions: How long have you been repaying the existing loan?
Are all repayments up to date?
needs.approved_framing: A top-up can combine the existing balance and new borrowing into one replacement loan.

needs.name: Finance third-level education
clarifying_questions: Is the course undergraduate or postgraduate?
Is it full-time and in Ireland?
needs.approved_framing: BOI has student borrowing options with eligibility tied to the course and student account relationship.

needs.name: Flexible card-based credit
clarifying_questions: Do you expect to clear the balance in full each month, or sometimes carry it?
What will you mainly use the card for?
needs.approved_framing: A credit card is revolving credit, so it is a different tool from a structured personal loan.
suppressions: Do not present as an emergency-fund substitute if the customer is in persistent financial difficulty.

needs.name: Travel-reward credit card
clarifying_questions: How often do you fly with Aer Lingus?
Would you use the card enough for the travel benefits to matter?
needs.approved_framing: If Aer Lingus travel is already part of your normal spending pattern, the travel-reward card may be worth comparing with the standard cards.

needs.name: Lower-rate credit card priority

signals.text: I sometimes carry a card balance

clarifying_questions: How often do you expect to carry a balance?
Are you comfortable with an annual fee if the overall product suits you?
needs.approved_framing: The relevant comparison is total card cost and usage, not simply rewards.

needs.name: College affinity card

signals.text: support my college through card spend

clarifying_questions: Which participating college are you interested in?
needs.approved_framing: An affinity card links everyday card use with support for a participating college.

needs.name: Student credit card

signals.text: need a small card while at college

clarifying_questions: Do you hold a BOI third-level current account?
Are you currently a full-time student or eligible recent graduate?
needs.approved_framing: There is a student-oriented credit-card route subject to account and eligibility requirements.

needs.name: Spread a large existing card purchase

signals.text: large purchase on my BOI card

clarifying_questions: Was the purchase at least €250?
Is it on an eligible personal BOI credit card?
needs.approved_framing: If the purchase is already on an eligible BOI card, an instalment plan may be more relevant than taking a separate loan.

needs.name: Buy first home
clarifying_questions: Are you buying alone or with someone?
Is it the first home for every applicant?
Have you found a property or are you working out affordability?
needs.approved_framing: We can start with affordability and the mortgage, then bring in deposit saving, protection and home insurance at the right stage.

needs.name: Move to another home
clarifying_questions: Do you currently have a mortgage?
Is your existing mortgage with BOI?
Are you selling your current home?
needs.approved_framing: This is a moving-home journey rather than a first-time buyer journey; existing mortgage context matters.

needs.name: Switch existing mortgage
clarifying_questions: Who is your current lender?
What is your approximate balance, property value and remaining term?
needs.approved_framing: We can explore whether moving your existing mortgage to BOI is relevant before discussing rates or application steps.

needs.name: Build or substantially renovate a home
clarifying_questions: Do you already own the site?
Do you have planning permission?
What stage is the build at?
needs.approved_framing: A self-build mortgage releases funds in stages, so it is a different journey from buying a completed home.

needs.name: Buy an investment property
clarifying_questions: Will this property be rented out rather than used as your main home?
needs.approved_framing: Investment-property borrowing is a separate mortgage need and should be treated distinctly from buying a home to live in.

needs.name: Borrow against existing home equity

signals.text: large renovation and I have equity

clarifying_questions: What is your approximate property value and mortgage balance?
What do you want the additional borrowing for?
needs.approved_framing: For larger needs, borrowing against available home equity may be worth comparing with unsecured borrowing.
suppressions: Do not present without acknowledging that the borrowing is secured on the home.

needs.name: Energy-efficient home / mortgage pricing
clarifying_questions: Do you know the property's BER?
needs.approved_framing: The home's BER may affect which BOI mortgage pricing options are available.
notes: Treat as pricing overlay, not a standalone customer goal.

needs.name: Protect home and contents
clarifying_questions: Do you need buildings cover, contents cover, or both?
Are you buying, renting, or a landlord?
needs.approved_framing: Home insurance can protect the building, belongings, or both depending on your situation.

needs.name: Protect upcoming travel
clarifying_questions: Is this one trip or do you travel several times a year?
Where are you going and what activities are planned?
needs.approved_framing: Single-trip and annual cover solve different travel patterns; destination and activities can also matter.

needs.name: Protect dependants financially

signals.text: my family relies on my income

clarifying_questions: Who depends financially on your income?
Do you already have any personal or employer-provided cover?
needs.approved_framing: If other people rely on your income, we can explore ways of protecting the household if something happens to you.
suppressions: Do not infer a protection sale directly from a health diagnosis or bereavement disclosure.

needs.name: Protect a main-home mortgage
clarifying_questions: Do you already have suitable mortgage protection in place?
needs.approved_framing: Mortgage protection is normally part of getting a main-home mortgage ready for drawdown.

needs.name: Protect income if unable to work
clarifying_questions: What sick pay or income protection do you already have through work?
How long could your household manage without your income?
needs.approved_framing: Income protection is designed to replace part of your income if illness or injury prevents you working.
suppressions: Do not infer from a disclosed illness; only surface from expressed resilience/protection need.

needs.name: Financial resilience to specified serious illness

signals.text: how would we cope financially if I became seriously ill

clarifying_questions: Do you already have this cover through work or another policy?
What financial commitments would be hardest to meet?
needs.approved_framing: Specified illness cover can provide a lump sum if a covered condition is diagnosed.
suppressions: Never treat a customer's actual diagnosis as a sales trigger.

needs.name: Start retirement saving

signals.text: need to start saving for retirement

clarifying_questions: Do you have any workplace pension already?
Roughly when would you like to retire?
needs.approved_framing: We can start by understanding what retirement you want and what provision you already have, then look at the appropriate pension route.

needs.name: Review existing retirement provision

signals.text: I have a pension but don't know if it's enough
am I on track for retirement

clarifying_questions: What pension arrangements do you already have?
What retirement income would you ideally want?
needs.approved_framing: A pension review is about whether your existing provision is on track before deciding whether anything should change.

needs.name: Turn pension savings into retirement income

signals.text: what do I do with my pension at retirement

clarifying_questions: When are you retiring?
Is secure regular income or flexibility more important to you?
needs.approved_framing: At retirement, income security, flexibility and access become the key trade-offs; this should move into an advice-led retirement conversation.

needs.name: Invest long-term surplus cash

signals.text: money I won't need for 5+ years
want to invest a lump sum

clarifying_questions: When might you need this money?
Do you have accessible emergency savings already?
How would you feel if the value fell for a period?
needs.approved_framing: If the money is genuinely long-term and you can accept investment risk, we can start the investment suitability journey.
suppressions: Suppress if the money is needed in the short/medium term.
Suppress if the customer has no reasonable accessible emergency reserve.
Do not recommend a specific investment before the suitability/advice process.

needs.name: Invest regularly for a long-term goal
clarifying_questions: What is the goal and time horizon?
How much can you commit regularly without needing access?
How comfortable are you with market fluctuations?
needs.approved_framing: For long horizons, investing may be worth exploring alongside or instead of cash saving, subject to affordability and risk.
suppressions: Do not present as guaranteed growth.

needs.name: Send or receive money internationally
clarifying_questions: Which country and currency?
How much are you sending or receiving?
Is this one-off or regular?
needs.approved_framing: BOI can support international and foreign-currency payments; whether you also need to hold the currency is a separate question.
